heard: Jupiter's giant storm once swallowed three Earth side by side. Even after shrinking for a century, it still swallows Earth whole. Winds around the edge roar past 200 miles per hour. It plunges 250 kilometers deep into Jupiter's dense atmosphere. Without a solid surface below, nothing creates friction to stop it. It survives by cannibalizing smaller, passing storms like atmospheric prey. When those smaller storms thin out, this monster begins to starve. Massive red fragments peeled away from its perimeter in 2019, yet deep inside, the solar system's largest storm keeps churning.
